methodology.title: Model Architecture
methodology.text: Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure [5,2,35].Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x 1 , ..., x n ) to a sequence of continuous representations z = (z 1 , ..., z n ).Given z, the decoder then generates an output sequence (y 1 , ..., y m ) of symbols one element at a time.At each step the model is auto-regressive [10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder, shown in the left and right halves of Figure 1, respectively.
methodology.full_text: Most competitive neural sequence transduction models have an encoder-decoder structure [5,2,35].Here, the encoder maps an input sequence of symbol representations (x 1 , ..., x n ) to a sequence of continuous representations z = (z 1 , ..., z n ).Given z, the decoder then generates an output sequence (y 1 , ..., y m ) of symbols one element at a time.At each step the model is auto-regressive [10], consuming the previously generated symbols as additional input when generating the next.The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder, shown in the left and right halves of Figure 1, respectively.

The Transformer achieves better BLEU scores than previous state-of-the-art models on the English-to-German and English-to-French newstest2014 tests at a fraction of the training cost.

Variations on the Transformer architecture.Unlisted values are identical to those of the base model.All metrics are on the English-to-German translation development set, newstest2013.Listed perplexities are per-wordpiece, according to our byte-pair encoding, and should not be compared to per-word perplexities.
